verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 5, 10, 16, 19 show a bare, flat, poured-concrete rooftop with a parapet wall running around the perimeter; no tiles, sheeting, or slope visible anywhere on the roof surface.
verdicts.rationale: Multiple independent rooftop photos consistently show a flat RCC-type terrace, directly matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5-6 site-layout diagrams and page 10-11 photos show plastic water tanks and a small equipment corner on the roof, but they are placed in a corner clearly outside the marked 'Proposed PV modules' array area; the rest of the roof (page 10, 16) is open and clear.
verdicts.rationale: A water tank exists on the roof but the layout diagrams and photos show it positioned away from the panel array, so it does not appear to obstruct the installation.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: The roof is flat RCC and the elevated mounting structure that would create the 10° tilt has not been installed yet (page 10, 16 show bare concrete only); only stylised CAD renderings (page 5-6) depict a tilted array, not an actual photo.
verdicts.rationale: No physical mounting structure or panel is visible in the site photos to visually confirm a 10° tilt; only a schematic rendering exists.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: All rooftop photos (pages 8, 10, 11, 16, 19) show a single continuous flat terrace with one parapet boundary; no separate roof planes or additional rooftop levels are visible.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: The AC cable (purple overlay) is traced consistently from the 'PV modules' label on the roof (page 11) through a wall/floor hole with real black cables visible on the ground (page 12), along ceiling/corridor corners (pages 13-14), and terminating at the 'Main meter'/'Solar meter' labels (page 15). Separately, the earthing run (orange/green overlay) is traced from the roof LA mount (page 16) through another wall hole (page 17), along a corridor wall (page 18), to the AC/DC/LA earth pit markers (page 19). Each page's route overlay begins near where the previous page's overlay ended, with captions ('Cable Routing', 'Earthing Routing') and 'Hole' markers explaining each wall penetration.
verdicts.rationale: The color-coded overlays for both the AC/DC cable run and the separate earthing run form a logically continuous path from roof to ground-floor termination across the sequential photos, with wall-penetration points explicitly called out and no visually orphaned/dangling cable ends; confidence is medium rather than high because continuity is inferred from overlay-line hand-offs between separate photos rather than one unbroken shot.
